runs.text:
The map of our solar system has changed.
For most of history, we viewed our neighborhood as a tidy, organized place. We thought it was a simple system with eight planets orbiting a star, surrounded by a clean void. 

We assumed there was a clear finish line where the solar system stopped and "deep space" began.

The Kuiper Belt proves that this model is wrong.
The solar system does not have a hard edge. It does not just end. Instead, it fades away into the galaxy.

What we once thought was empty space is actually a massive, chaotic frontier. It is populated by billions of objects that are far more complex than we realized.
